STRAIGHT ANSWERS

A few things
you might be wondering.

Start with clarity about what happens next.

How we work ↗
What would I actually receive?

The proposed deliverable is a plain-English report showing the agreed scope, assessment date, evidence, limitations and prioritised actions with suggested owners. Unchecked systems and failed checks would be marked explicitly. See the fictional sample report for the format.

Are services and prices available now?

The service is in preparation. Figures shown are planning benchmarks, with scope, availability, VAT and commercial terms still to be confirmed. No payment is taken here.

Can you work with my existing IT provider?

Yes—the proposed review is designed to support your existing arrangements. The report would separate business decisions from technical tasks, so you can agree who handles each action. Any remediation would need a separate agreed scope.

Will you need confidential client records?

The first conversation does not require confidential customer records, client names, passwords or recovery codes. Any later access must be justified and agreed within the written scope.

Does a public observation mean my business is vulnerable?

No. A DNS record, missing website header or supplier reference needs context. It does not prove compromise, reveal private account settings or establish that a published vulnerability applies. The report format separates observations, matters requiring verification and checks that could not be completed.

Is Cyber Essentials certification included?

The planned service is preparation support. Certification is a separate assessment by an appropriate independent certification body; it is not awarded by Cyber Defender or guaranteed by a readiness review. Any certification fees would need to be confirmed separately.

Can I book a call online?

Yes. Book your 30-minute consultation on Calendly, choose an available date and time, then enter your name and email. See what we’ll discuss before you book.
